title: 2023年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 There are close to 58,000 homeless people in Los Angeles county. That's a shocking and tragic number for a region that's home to some of the richest people in the world. At last, the problem became so acute—and so visible—that Los Angeles took extraordinary action. The citizens of this county voted in November 2016 and again in March 2017 to raise their own taxes. The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar, 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless.

P2 As a result, Los Angeles now has its best chance in decades to combat homelessness. This is an opportunity that surely all can agree must not be wasted. It is neither desirable nor morally acceptable nor practical for this county to tolerate the signs of deprivation more commonly associated with the slums(贫民窟) of Rio de Janiero.

P3 How did we get here? For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition—to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. But contrary to popular belief, the homeless in Los Angeles are not mostly mentally ill or drug addicted or frightening, although a sizable minority meet some of those descriptions. Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them—they lost a job or were evicted(逐出) or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving.

P4 The challenges are enormous, even if everyone is pulling in the same direction. That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing.

P5 In the world's richest nation, homelessness on this scale should be shameful and shocking. But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. Compassion(同情心) is being replaced by resignation.

questions.q: Why did the citizens of Los Angeles vote to raise their own taxes?
options: To combat the county's homelessness.
To reform the county's service system.
To fund the development of local infrastructure.
To narrow the gap between the rich and the poor.
questions.explain:
【判型】Q51 针对"市民投票加税"这一文中明确发生的事件追问原因，答案是文中写死的事实，不需 要推理。

【拆句】Q51 是一个标准疑问句，主干为 Why did the citizens vote to raise their own taxes，其 中 to raise their own taxes 是不定式作 vote 的目的，整句结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar, 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless. 此举的目的是资助一项数十亿美元、为期十年、面向无家可归者的住房与社会服务计划。 51. Why did the citizens of Los Angeles vote to raise their own taxes? A) To combat the county's homelessness. B) To reform the county's service system. C) To fund the development of local infrastructure. D) To narrow the gap between the rich and the poor.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 housing and social services for the homeless ↔combat the county's homelessness The purpose of such action ↔To combat 预判"为无家可归者出钱解决问题"与 To combat the county's homelessness 完全吻 合，故锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文只说资助住房与社会服务，从未提"改革服务体系"，reform the county's service system 是凭 services 一词臆造出的动作。 C) 偷换概念 加税资助的是 housing and social services，the development of local infrastructure 把"住房与社会服务"偷换成"地方基础设施建设"，二者并非一回事。 D) 无中生有 原文 some of the richest people in the world 只是用富裕反衬问题之刺眼，从未说 加税是为"缩小贫富差距"，narrow the gap between the rich and the poor 属臆造 目的。 人们往往对无家可归者持什么看法? A) 他们很少符合无家可归的描述。 B) 他们是经济快速发展的受害者。 C) 他们应该为自己的处境负责。 D) 他们占吸毒成瘾者的大多数。

questions.q: What do people tend to believe about the homeless?
options: They seldom meet the descriptions of homelessness.
They are the victims of fast economic development.
They are responsible for their own condition.
They account for the majority of drug addicts.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do people tend to believe 问的是文中明确描述过的一种社会观念，原文有现成陈 述，属事实细节而非作者本人观点的推断。

【拆句】Q52 主干为 What do people tend to believe about the homeless，tend to believe 是"倾向于相信"的固定搭配，about the homeless 限定讨论对象，结构简单无陷阱。

【定位】For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition—to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. 只要有无家可归者存在，就有一种倾向，把他们的处境归咎于受害者自身——把他们的潦倒 看作品格、道德缺陷或懒惰的问题。 52. What do people tend to believe about the homeless? A) They seldom meet the descriptions of homelessness. B) They are the victims of fast economic development. C) They are responsible for their own condition. D) They account for the majority of drug addicts.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说无家可归者"多数并非"精神病或瘾君子，是作者驳斥偏见，seldom meet the descriptions 把"少数符合"歪曲成"很少符合"，且这是作者观点而非"人们倾向相信"的 内容。 B) 答非所问 victims of fast economic development 把原文 the economy forgot them（被经济 遗忘）偷换成"快速经济发展的受害者"，且这是作者给出的真实成因，并非题干所问 的"人们倾向相信"的偏见。 C) ✓ 正确 blame the victims themselves for their condition ↔responsible for their own condition the victims themselves ↔their own 预判"责任在他们自己"与 They are responsible for their own condition 直接对应，故 锁定。 D) 以偏概全 原文只说"相当一部分人"符合吸毒等描述，account for the majority of drug addicts 反过来说无家可归者"占瘾君子的大多数"，既夸大又颠倒了主从关系。 洛杉矶越来越多的人无家可归的原因之一是什么? A) 他们发现越来越难以负担住处。 B) 该县的离婚率一直在稳步上升。 C) 他们被迫从事低薪工作。 D) 社会未能原谅他们的过错。

questions.q: What is one of the causes for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless?
options: They find it increasingly difficult to afford a place to live.
The divorce rate in the county has been on a steady rise.
They have been compelled to take low-paying jobs.
The society fails to forgive them for their mistakes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one of the causes 用 one of 限定，只需在原文列举的若干成因里找出与某个选项 对得上的那一个，是定位细节而非推断。

【拆句】Q53 主干为 What is one of the causes，for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless 是介词 for 引导的长定语，修饰 causes，说明"什么的成因"；拆开后 即"越来越多洛杉矶人沦为无家可归者"的成因，理清这层修饰即无障碍。

【定位】Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them—they lost a job or were evicted or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving. 如今，越来越多流落街头的人是因为坏运气、一连串失误，或因为被经济遗忘——他们失 业、被逐出住所或逃离虐待性婚姻，恰逢房市变得越来越无情。 53. What is one of the causes for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless? A) They find it increasingly difficult to afford a place to live. B) The divorce rate in the county has been on a steady rise. C) They have been compelled to take low-paying jobs. D) The society fails to forgive them for their mistakes.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving ↔ increasingly difficult to afford a place to live 预判"房市苛刻让人难有住处"与 They find it increasingly difficult to afford a place to live 吻合，故锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文只提个别人 fled an abusive marriage（逃离虐待婚姻），是个体经历，从未说"全 郡离婚率持续上升"，divorce rate … on a steady rise 属臆造统计趋势。 C) 无中生有 原文说有人 lost a job（失业），并未说他们被迫去做低薪工作，compelled to take low-paying jobs 与文意不符且属臆造。 D) 偷换概念 原文 unforgiving 形容的是 housing market（房市无情），society fails to forgive them for their mistakes 把"房市"偷换成"社会"、把"无情"曲解为"不原谅错误"，张冠 李戴式偷换。 我们从洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局的新报告中了解到什么? A) 为无家可归者提供足够的就业机会仍然是一个挑战。 B) 每个人都在朝着同一个方向努力解决无家可归问题。 C) 新增住房的增长远远满足不了不断增长的无家可归人口的需求。 D) 洛杉矶的无家可归状况恶化速度比许多人预测的要快。

questions.q: What do we learn from the new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report?
options: Supplying enough job opportunities for the homeless remains a challenge.
Everyone is pulling in the same direction to solve the homelessness problem.
The increase in new housing falls short of the demand of the growing homeless population.
Los Angeles' homeless condition is deteriorating faster than many people predict.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the new … report 问一份具名报告的内容，答案就是报告所陈述 的事实，回原文读该报告对应句即可。

【拆句】Q54 主干为 What do we learn from the report，new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority 是一长串前置定语修饰 report，看着唬人，实为"洛杉矶无家可归者服务局的新 报告"，拆掉定语主干极简，无陷阱。

【定位】That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing. 本月一份新的洛杉矶无家可归者服务局报告印证了这一现实：本郡无家可归人口的增长速度 快于新住房的供给速度。 54. What do we learn from the new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report? A) Supplying enough job opportunities for the homeless remains a challenge. B) Everyone is pulling in the same direction to solve the homelessness problem. C) The increase in new housing falls short of the demand of the growing homeless population. D) Los Angeles' homeless condition is deteriorating faster than many people predict.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 报告比较的是"人口"与"住房"，Supplying enough job opportunities 把"住房供给"偷 换成"就业机会供给"，报告未涉及就业。 B) 答非所问 Everyone is pulling in the same direction 取自报告前一句 even if everyone is pulling in the same direction，那是作者的假设语气，并非报告内容，题干问的是"报 告说了什么"。 C) ✓ 正确 the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing ↔ The increase in new housing falls short of the demand of the growing homeless population the supply of new housing ↔The increase in new housing 预判"住房供给跟不上需求"与 The increase in new housing falls short of the demand 完全对应，故锁定。 D) 无中生有 报告只说人口增长快于住房供给，从未提"恶化速度快于许多人的预测"，faster than many people predict 凭空加入"预测"这一参照，属臆造。 大多数洛杉矶居民现在对无家可归问题有何感受? A) 他们对其规模感到越来越羞愧。 B) 他们发现它并不像看起来那么可怕。 C) 他们对此越来越不冷漠。 D) 他们不再觉得震惊。

questions.q: How do most Los Angeles residents now feel about homelessness?
options: They are increasingly ashamed about its scale.
They find it no more scaring than it appears.
They are less and less indifferent to it.
They no longer find it shocking.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do most Los Angeles residents now feel 看似问态度，但原文末段把居民的感受逐 词列了出来，答案能逐字对应，按细节题回原文核对即可，无需揣摩作者立场。

【拆句】Q55 主干为 How do residents feel about homelessness，now 是关键时间状语，强 调"如今"而非过去，提醒答案要选"当下"的感受；句子结构简单，唯一要抓的是这个时间 限定。

【定位】But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. 但多数洛杉矶居民已不再震惊，也不再羞愧。我们越来越多地感到不适、恼火、厌恶、害怕 或浑然不觉。 55. How do most Los Angeles residents now feel about homelessness? A) They are increasingly ashamed about its scale. B) They find it no more scaring than it appears. C) They are less and less indifferent to it. D) They no longer find it shocking.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说居民 no longer … shamed（不再羞愧），increasingly ashamed 说"越来越羞 愧"，与原文正相反。 B) 与原文相反 原文把 scared（害怕）列为居民如今增多的情绪之一，no more scaring than it appears 却说"不比看上去更可怕"，与原文相反。 C) 与原文相反 原文说居民越来越 unaware（漠然），同情 being replaced by resignation（被无奈 取代），less and less indifferent 说"越来越不漠然"，与原文趋势相反。 D) ✓ 正确 most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed ↔ They no longer find it shocking 预判"不再震惊"与 They no longer find it shocking 逐词吻合，故锁定。
